title: More frequent buses
summary: Adds Chapel Hill Transit service, so buses come more often.

decider.body: Chapel Hill Town Council, with Carrboro and UNC (Chapel Hill Transit's funding partners)
how: Chapel Hill Transit staff propose the added service and its cost.
The funding partners agree how to split the cost.
Town Council approves the Town's share in the budget.

evidence.claim: Bus ridership rises roughly 0.5% per 1% more service
evidence.source: TCRP Report 95, Chapter 9: Transit Scheduling and Frequency

evidence.claim: Chapel Hill Transit carried 4.3M trips in 2025; transit fund $36.5M

pros: Shorter waits draw some commuters out of cars, which also speeds up the roads and widens access to jobs.
cons: The Town pays its share of the cost of the added service, every year it runs.
Ridership grows less than service: about 0.5% per 1% more service in the studies cited.
